intended_object: The block-diagonal reflection matrix diag(I, −I) on ℝ^ι ⊕ ℝ^ι, which negates the second (imaginary) block of coordinates. Under realification, entrywise complex conjugation of a matrix becomes congruence by this matrix. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body is `Matrix.fromBlocks 1 0 0 (-1)` on `ι ⊕ ι` over ℝ. That is exactly the identity on the `inl` block and minus the identity on the `inr` block, so it is the reflection the docstring describes. The proofs that follow in the file match this: it is symmetric, it is its own inverse, and its determinant is a unit.

The definition is real-valued and uses the same index type ι for both blocks. This is not too narrow. The object is specific: the matrix that negates the imaginary coordinates of a realification `!![Re A, -Im A; Im A, Re A]`. Its role needs the real scalar field and the two copies of the same index type.

Mathlib has the more general `LieAlgebra.Orthogonal.indefiniteDiagonal p q R`, which is `diagonal (Sum.elim 1 (-1))` over any commutative ring with possibly different index types. Our matrix is that one with p = q = ι and R = ℝ, written with blocks instead of a diagonal. The difference is only a matter of formulation and does not matter here.
